title: 1700s Naval Game Looking for anyone interested in testing & feedback
author: PhotoDisastrous8275
selftext:
I'd like to start off by saying thank you to everyone who has contributed feedback from my last 2 post.

I'm looking for anyone interested in the genre that I can connect with to have you play the current build and provide feedback on what should change and what should be refined more.

comments.author: Jonotr0n
comments.body: I’m developing something similar, Caribbean in 1795. Did you use the sea of thieves method to create your waves?

replies.author: PhotoDisastrous8275
replies.body: Sea of thieves method ? I haven’t looked into it. What is it

replies.author: Jonotr0n
replies.body: Sea of Thieves uses a physically based FFT ocean (Jerry Tessendorf’s “Simulating Ocean Water” method), which adds up thousands of waves at once, each moving at its natural speed and pushed sideways into sharp crests. On top of that is stylised shading: a blend of a deep colour and a lighter “light through the crests” colour based on view angle, sun direction and wave peaks. Foam is generated at the wave peaks and around objects cutting the surface, held in a buffer that’s blurred a little more each frame so it spreads and softens, then blended with hand-painted foam textures. It’s realistic wave motion with a cartoon paint job, all covered in Rare’s SIGGRAPH 2018 talk, “The Technical Art of Sea of Thieves”.
